## Final Accepted Amendments

### `fr-1-947a9f46`

In `budget_helpers.rs`, the four `partial_cmp().unwrap()` calls (lines 139, 242, 305, 450) will panic if any budget delta value is NaN. Replace `.unwrap()` with `.unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)` in all four locations (`largest_mover`, `assert_o2_balanced` worst-tick finder, `assert_budget_balanced` worst-tick finder, and `largest_mover_in_tick`). NaN values are unlikely in normal operation but can arise from division-by-zero bugs elsewhere in the simulation; the assertion helpers should degrade gracefully with a diagnostic rather than panic with a confusing `unwrap` backtrace.

### `fr-1-53770879`

The acceptance criterion states 'the helpers compile without overhead when budget tracking is disabled'. The current implementation uses runtime `Option` checks rather than a compile-time feature flag. This meets the spirit of the requirement (no snapshot computation or allocation when `budget_ledger` is `None`), but should be explicitly documented in the module-level docs or AGENTS.md that 'disabled' means runtime opt-out via `Option<BudgetLedger>`, not a cargo feature gate. Currently the budget_helpers module doc says nothing about the zero-cost mechanism.

### `fr-1-3d3b6612`

In `types/budget.rs` line 102, `BudgetTotals::from_state` clamps dissolved oxygen to zero with `.max(0.0)`. If DO goes negative due to a bug in the oxygen system, this silently hides the issue and makes the budget appear balanced when it isn't. Add a `debug_assert!(state.water.dissolved_oxygen_mg_total >= -f64::EPSILON)` before the clamp, or log a warning, so that negative DO is caught during development while still producing a valid total for the budget system.

### `fr-1-5c021677`

`crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs:177-188` only emits `TANK_BUDGET_DEBUG` output after `engine.step_hours(hours)` succeeds. If stepping fails after one or more successful ticks, those completed ticks have already been recorded in the ledger (`crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:254-255`), but `step_and_inspect` returns early and prints nothing. That makes the new debug hook useless in the exact failure mode it is supposed to help diagnose. Print newly recorded ticks on the error path too, or otherwise surface the partial inspection data before returning the error.

### `fr-1-80582d62`

`crates/tank_core/tests/water_change_mass_balance.rs:16-30` now calls `systems::water_change::apply_water_change` directly instead of queueing `PlayerAction::WaterChangePercent` and stepping the engine. That bypasses the public integration path in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:435-460`, so this test no longer covers queue draining, action processing order, source-profile lookup through the engine, or any invariant/budget interaction attached to the real action. Keep the fixture isolated from atmospheric exchange if needed, but preserve at least one assertion that exercises `engine.apply_action(...); engine.step_hours(1)`.

### `fr-1-2448ab6a`

The new helper API is still only exercised from the dedicated synthetic file `crates/tank_core/tests/budget_helpers.rs:136-154`; the existing shrimp conservation tests in `crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_feeding_pathway.rs:206-234` continue to hand-roll `total_nitrogen()` / `total_carbon()` before-after checks even though this bead introduced `step_and_inspect` plus one-line assertions. That leaves the acceptance criterion about retrofitting an existing test unmet and misses an integration point showing future authors how to use the helper in a real scenario test. Convert one of those existing conservation tests to `step_and_inspect` + `assert_n_conserved` / `assert_c_conserved`.
